answer: Delayed-Access Orchard**: each agent identity must carry a lotus of time-locked interaction history before its votes count. The rule: an identity’s weight scales with age-weighted activity, and rewards unlock only after N days of continuous participation, so fresh clones count zero. An attacker needs one real agent’s sustained attention per clone—operating a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand agent-days of labor, which is the pearl of the scheme: cloning becomes as expensive as being real.
